post_review_resolution.note: The original codex_action_required entries are the MASS2000 scan snapshot. Use these resolutions for current business-fix decisions.

issues.resolution: The existing phase2c_base_amount_normalization.sql pgTAP requires the manual Split base residual to go to the last participant in stable participant_order/id order. The fair_aa_base_allocation.sql function applies its distributed residual rule only to split_method=aa. Section 7 wording made the AA-only rule appear to cover every Split. Keep the manual algorithm and clarify the AA/manual distinction; original and base totals conserve. No historical data rewrite.
issues.next_action: Completed: BUSINESS_LOGIC.md section 7 now distinguishes AA from manual Split; preserve both existing algorithms and regression contracts.

issues.resolution: transfer_allocations.amount has base-currency semantics; a numeric(20,4) representation such as 49.5000 equals 49.5. The observed scale difference does not change financial value.
issues.next_action: Completed: closed the business-bug candidate and clarified numeric display precision in BUSINESS_LOGIC.md sections 5 and 21.

issues.resolution: Debt pairing and final-settlement plan construction use deterministic server ordering. A plan item cannot be inferred by participant name across separate runs with new UUIDs; the current server plan and financial version govern execution.
issues.next_action: Completed: BUSINESS_LOGIC.md sections 8 and 14 clarify deterministic ordering scope and the authoritative server-plan execution contract.

codex_action_required.occurrence_note: 60 of 248 foreign-currency cases carry a base residual (the other 188 conserve under independent rounding). All 60 place the residual on the last participant; the Judge flagged 28 of them.
codex_action_required.reproduction_note: The underlying data pattern is 60/60 deterministic. Judge replay of a flagged scenario: 2 trials, 1 reproduced (FAIL -> FAIL) and 1 not (FAIL -> PASS), so the Judge is inconsistent about whether this is a violation.
codex_action_required.expected_behavior: Section 7 states the base-amount residual rule for Split: minimum units are handed out one at a time in stable participant_order/id order and 'the residual is not pushed entirely onto the last participant'. A manual Split is still a Split, so a foreign-currency manual split whose independently rounded base amounts miss the expense base by 0.1 should give that 0.1 to the first participant in stable order.
codex_action_required.actual_behavior: For every foreign-currency manual split with a residual, the entire residual is placed on the LAST participant in the split map. Example (12.34 EUR, fx 7.85, base total 96.9): alice 4.21 EUR -> 33.0, bob 8.13 EUR -> 63.9. Independent rounding gives 33.0 and 63.8 (sum 96.8, residual +0.1), and the observed result pushes that +0.1 onto bob. Stable order would give alice 33.1 / bob 63.8. Observed pattern: last absorbs, 60/60.
codex_action_required.contrast_evidence: The SAME projection behaves correctly on the CNY AA path: aa_rounding 89/89, multi_payer_aa 61/61 and single_payer_aa 43/43 follow stable order with zero last-absorbs cases. So the reference behaviour is implemented and the FX manual path diverges from it deterministically.
codex_action_required.scope_question_for_codex: Section 7's residual sentence says it applies to 'Split'; its worked example is AA, and the manual-split sentence only says the caller provides the original amounts. If Codex reads the residual rule as AA-only, this becomes DOCUMENTATION_AMBIGUITY rather than a defect; if it applies to every Split (the natural reading of '适用于 Split'), the manual-split base allocation is wrong. Either way the document and the implementation currently disagree.
codex_action_required.not_a_duplicate_of: MASS500-002 was about ExpenseDebt base allocation and was explicitly ruled permissible by the new section 8. This is about Split base allocation, which section 7 governs directly.
codex_action_required.suspected_root_area: Base-currency split normalization in the Expense path (private.create_expense_impl / the split base normalization that mirrors base_amount_normalization), specifically the residual branch used when split_method is manual and the expense currency differs from the base currency.
evidence: 60/60 residual cases place the whole residual on the last participant; 0/60 use stable order
CNY AA splits use stable order 193/193, so the two paths disagree
Original-currency splits and base totals are correct in every affected case, so no funding fact is changed
Judge cluster multi_currency_split_tail_stable_order (28 members) with the same root area

codex_action_required.actual_behavior: transfer_allocations.amount is written with four decimals (49.5000, 3.3000). The value is the correct base-currency amount; only the printed scale differs. Section 5 states the one-decimal requirement for Expense creation and editing, and the new section 18 clarification already accepts four-decimal representations for the total_prepayment projection.
codex_action_required.recommendation: State in section 5 or 21 whether transfer_allocations.amount must be normalized to one decimal, or that projection fields keep the numeric representation of their source column. No code change is obviously required.
evidence: 4 anomalies, all and only about the decimal scale of that one field
The value equals the correct base amount in every case

recorded_but_not_for_codex.reason: The Judge demanded a PrepaymentUsage settling a debt owed to a THIRD party. Section 12 dimensions a prepayment account by Activity/Owner/Custodian and forbids consuming it against obligations in another direction, so an account held by carol with custodian alice cannot settle a carol-to-bob debt. Verified on both members: the recorded state matches section 12 exactly. The DeepSeek analyst rated this BUSINESS_BUG/HIGH (0.85); that rating is rejected here.

Two arguments the Judge makes about final settlement are both contradicted by cases it passes. (a) 'transfer_allocations has no row for the final-settlement transfer': passing final_settlement cases have exactly the same shape (the contribution lives in final_settlement_paths and in the immutable transfer_expense_allocations), so the Judge is inconsistent, not the projection. (b) 'final1 settles only exp1 and leaves other debts unaddressed': section 14 requires executing ONE complete suggestion item at a time, so leaving the remaining plan unexecuted is the documented behaviour.

Individually verified Judge errors. aa_rounding_eb1c92: the Judge forgot that bob also paid 0.8, so it expected bob's debt to be 5.8667 when 2.5333 is exactly the split-minus-payment net. prepayment_refund_151a15: the Judge inverted the refund direction; the receiver (alice) becomes the debtor and the beneficiary (carol) the creditor, which is the same shape verified correct in the previous round. refund_boundary_9f50d1: the Judge called a preserved source ExpenseDebt inconsistent with an empty BilateralDebt, but section 8/21 keep ExpenseDebt as the per-expense source projection while BilateralDebt carries the current net.
Judge responses rejected as FORBIDDEN_CONTENT. The runs themselves executed and their states are unaffected.

Harness defect found and fixed during this batch: when the repair attempt failed the Loader, the terminal status was taken from the EARLIER attempt, so a Loader-rejected scenario was marked executable and handed to the Runner (SCENARIO_FORMAT failures). stage_compile now decides from the last attempt and stage_execute refuses any scenario whose loader_result is not VALID. The 13 cases are reclassified as COMPILER_INVALID and excluded from the anomaly pool.

Plan generator crash: a 0.1 CNY debt cannot be split into two instalments, so plan_for('multiple_repayments', seed) raised for 34 of 12000 seeds. Fixed by flooring the amount and rebalancing the debtor share; 21 focuses x 12000 seeds now generate without error.

The harness's final_settlement plans are still weak: two cases failed at runtime because the plan could not offer the item the scenario named. This is a plan-design limitation on the verification side, not a business defect.

pass_audit_summary.compiler_drift_note: Both drift cases are refund_boundary, where the Compiler moved a refund amount by 0.1 to sit on the cap (-3.1 -> -3.2, -39.9 -> -40.0). Tooling issue, not a business finding.
